goals.1: Describing a festival from your own country
goals.2: obwohl clauses: verb at the end
dialog.5.de.4.n: obwohl clause: verb at the end
grammar.0.title: Public holidays in Germany (Feiertage)
grammar.0.note: The holidays differ a little from state to state. On a public holiday shops and offices are closed — do your shopping the day before.
grammar.1.title: obwohl clause: verb at the end
grammar.1.text: obwohl = although. It starts a subordinate clause, so the verb goes at the end. It expresses a contrary result.
grammar.2.title: weil / obwohl / wenn / dass — compared
grammar.2.note: All four start a subordinate clause: the verb goes right at the end. When the subordinate clause comes first, the main clause starts with the verb: „Obwohl ich müde bin, arbeite ich.“
quiz.6.why: When the subordinate clause comes first → the main clause starts with the verb.
quiz.7.prompt: What is the holiday on 1 May called?
quiz.8.why: The last day of the year.
quiz.9.prompt: Put the sentence in order: “Although I am tired, I work.”
quiz.9.why: Subordinate clause first → the main clause starts with the verb.
